extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers and practitioners studying LLM transparency, privacy, and data leakage
extracted.subtask_description: A survey and experimental study that defines and measures transparency-related metrics for large language models (LLMs), and proposes a few-shot self-detection method to detect training-data leakage for personal information, copyrighted text, and benchmark data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leakage rate
rubrics_metrics.description: the proportion of leaked data in training data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as the origin of data leakage issues. The paper notes that although leakage rate is the source of leakage problems, it is not well understood how it affects the output rate and detection rate; experiments vary leakage rate to study its effect on different leaked content types (personal information, copyrighted texts, benchmarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Output rate
rubrics_metrics.description: the ease of generating leaked data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalized as how readily an LLM produces leaked information given prompts. Measured using a dataset of prompts designed to elicit personal information, copyrighted text, and benchmarks. Empirical finding: LLMs often produce leaked information even when the proportion of such data in training is small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection rate
rubrics_metrics.description: the detection performance of leaked versus non-leaked data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates methods' ability to distinguish instances present in the training data from those absent. The paper compares detection performance across methods and introduces a learned few-shot self-detection approach that is reported to outperform existing (non-explicit-learning) detection methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-detection approach (few-shot learning)
rubrics_metrics.description: uses few-shot learning in which LLMs detect whether instances are present or absent in their training data, in contrast to previous methods that do not employ explicit learning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed as a detection method; presented and empirically validated against existing methods, showing superior detection performance. Serves as a methodological criterion for evaluating detection effectiveness in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt elicitation dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: a dataset of prompts designed to elicit personal information, copyrighted text, and benchmarks from LLMs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Created to probe the ease of generating leaked information and to standardize measurement of output rate across content types. Used for experimental evaluation of leakage and detection methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of leaked content evaluated
rubrics_metrics.description: personal information, copyrighted texts, and benchmark data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study focuses on these three categories as distinct kinds of leakage to be measured and compared. Experimental results and analyses are reported per content type to show differences/similarities in leakage and detectability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship analysis between leakage rate and output/detection rates
rubrics_metrics.description: experimental survey to elucidate how varying leakage rate affects output rate and detection rate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central analytical objective of the paper: to determine whether and how the proportion of leaked data in training influences (a) the ease of generating leaked content and (b) the ability to detect leaked versus non-leaked instances. Findings indicate small amounts of leaked data can greatly affect outputs and that the proposed self-detection method improves detection performance.
